title: Finding your sangha
hookLine: a temple, a center, a small group
tomorrow: three monks, one heavy water pot, no words. what happened?

lines: A ROOM WHERE YOU KNOW NO ONE.
A HOUSE COOKING FOR THE BUDDHA.
cards: Walking into a room where you know no one has its own cold: the club fair, a new lunch table, the first night at a gym. On Saturday Mai took two buses to Ông's old temple, got as far as the door, and nearly turned around.
A merchant named Anathapindika once did the same, in the dark. He's in another city on business, and his host's house is in an uproar, cooking for tomorrow. Who's coming, a king?
No, says the host: the Buddha and the sangha. The merchant has never heard the word Buddha said like that. He can't sleep.
Long before dawn, he gets up and walks out through the city gate.

teach.h: DARKNESS, FEAR, WANTING TO TURN BACK.
teach.b: Outside the walls, the light goes. The text says darkness came down on him, he was afraid, his hair stood on end, and he wanted to turn back.

Then a voice in the dark, a spirit, tells him that going forward is better for him than turning back. The light returns. He keeps walking, through a cool grove, toward a figure pacing in the open air at first light.
The Buddha calls him by his given name: come, Sudatta. That's the whole first meeting.
Cold, fear, a voice saying keep going, and being called by name. Here's what the story became.

teach.h: A GROVE GIVEN, A DOOR TO FIND.
teach.b: Anathapindika gave the sangha a place to stay near his own city, the Jeta Grove, a monastery the suttas name again and again. That's what Buddhist temples are for: a door the community can be found behind.
And it's why, even now, you walk in to the same small signs. Shoes left at the door. Incense.
A bell. People saying the refuges aloud: Buddham saranam gacchami, I go to the Buddha for refuge, then the Dhamma, then the Sangha. Fear at the door is old.
So is the advice: going forward is better.

how: Lay Buddhists find community at temples, meditation centers and small sitting groups; on entering a temple people often leave their shoes at the door, offer incense or flowers, and recite the three refuges together.

o: choosing the temple nearest to your home
walking toward the community that keeps the path
a test you pass to be accepted by the monks

games.q: the walk in the dark — tap the pairs.
p: the name the Buddha called him
a place he gave the sangha

s: Anathapindika walked to the Buddha calm and sure the whole way
the text says darkness fell, he was afraid, and he wanted to turn back.
the Buddha greeted him by his own given name
come, Sudatta: called by name at first light.
a Buddhist temple exists mainly to house statues
Anathapindika gave the sangha a place to stay; a temple is a door where the community can be found.

games.q: a friend just moved to a new city and wants a Buddhist group. she finds a temple, a meditation center and a living-room sit, and freezes. what fits today's story?
o: pick one and walk in; fear at the door is normal, and going forward is better.
wait until she feels completely ready, so the first visit isn't wasted.
only the temple counts, since a real sangha must have monks in the room.
games.why: Anathapindika was afraid and nearly turned back; the voice said going forward is better. any of the three can be the door.

practice: If you can, stand and walk a few slow steps across the room. Feel each foot land, the floor cool or warm under it, the weight shifting from one side to the other. With each step, remember the voice in the dark: going forward.
When you arrive somewhere, stand still a moment, then let the sit begin.

wordCard.voice: Finding your sangha: walking toward the people who keep the path, past the fear at the door.

orig.note: Pali: community; the third of the three refuges.

carryVoice: The line for today: find them, even when the door is the hardest part. Day fifteen of the block, walked.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 10.8 (Sudatta Sutta: Anathapindika's first meeting with the Buddha)
Vinaya Pitaka, Cullavagga VI.4 (Anathapindika and the gift of the Jeta Grove)
